concept.name: Database Indexing: B-Trees vs LSM-Trees
concept.tagline: Optimize query read latencies using balanced search trees or log-structured merge-tree write buffers.

spark.summary: Database indexes turn linear O(N) table scans into logarithmic O(log N) lookups. B-Trees optimize point & range reads; LSM-Trees turn random writes into sequential disk writes.
spark.keyTakeaway: Choose B-Trees for read-heavy workloads (PostgreSQL/MySQL) and LSM-Trees for write-heavy append workloads (Cassandra/RocksDB).

concept.whyItMatters: Without indexes, searching 10,000,000 rows requires scanning every byte on disk. Indexes keep sorted pointers in memory/disk structures.
whenToUse: High-cardinality foreign keys and primary keys.
Range queries on timestamp or numerical columns.
whenNotToUse: Tables with massive write-only volume where index update overhead slows ingestion.
keyPoints: B+ Trees store key-pointer pairs in self-balancing nodes; leaf nodes form a doubly-linked list for fast range scans.
LSM-Trees buffer writes in a MemTable (RAM) and write sequential SSTables to disk, compacting periodically.

examples.title: PostgreSQL B-Tree Index
examples.scenario: Finding user by email out of 5,000,000 users.

tradeOffs.con: LSM-Trees provide 10x higher write ingestion speed.

failureModes.name: Index Fragmentation
failureModes.description: Random updates leave empty page gaps.
failureModes.mitigation: Run periodic REINDEX / VACUUM FULL operations.

commonMistakes: Creating duplicate indexes on overlapping composite key columns.

caseStudy.problem: Ingesting 1M IoT sensor writes per second.
caseStudy.solution: Used LSM-Tree storage engine with Bloom Filters.
caseStudy.impact: Sub-millisecond write insertion without disk random seek bottlenecks.

relationships.description: Database indexes optimize disk lookups whereas caching stores results in RAM.

questions.title: B+ Tree vs LSM-Tree Storage Engine Trade-Offs
questions.prompt: Why do high-throughput write-heavy storage engines (like RocksDB and Cassandra) use LSM-Trees instead of traditional B+ Trees?

options.text: B+ Trees do not support string data types.
options.explanation: B+ Trees support arbitrary data types.

options.text: LSM-Trees buffer writes in memory (MemTable) and write sequential SSTables to disk, eliminating random disk seek overhead during writes.
options.explanation: Correct! LSM-Trees transform expensive random disk writes into cheap sequential appends.

rubric.excellent: Explains MemTable memory buffering, sequential SSTable writes, and avoidance of random I/O seeks.
rubric.gap: Thinks B+ trees cannot run on SSDs.

questions.sampleSolution: LSM-Trees buffer writes in RAM (MemTable) and write sequential SSTable files to disk, eliminating random disk write seeks.
questions.explanation: Sequential disk writes execute up to 100x faster than random page writes in B+ Trees under heavy insert volume.

interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: You are building a crypto transaction ledger storing 2,000,000 write events per second while supporting point-in-time range queries for balance auditing. How do you design the storage engine indexing strategy?

dimensions.name: Storage Engine Selection
dimensions.description: Choosing LSM-Tree with SSTable compaction for write throughput.

dimensions.name: Bloom Filter Read Optimization
dimensions.description: Using Bloom Filters to prevent unnecessary SSTable disk reads.

interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Use an LSM-Tree storage engine (RocksDB/Cassandra) for sequential disk write ingestion. Pair each SSTable with an in-memory Bloom Filter to eliminate disk reads for non-existent keys during balance lookups.
commonPitfalls: Using a single B+ Tree PostgreSQL table which locks under 2M writes/sec.
